newsitem.title: USA: N.J. Gov says to spend $250 mln more on schools.
newsitem.headline: N.J. Gov says to spend $250 mln more on schools.

text.p: New Jersey Gov. Christine Whitman said Tuesday she plans to comply in full with a state Supreme Court order requiring New Jersey to spend an additional $250 million on the poorest school districts.
Whitman said the budget hole created by the new spending would be manageable at $100 million if the Legislature agrees to her plan to borrow $2.8 billion for the state pension system.
The pension bond deal, which would be underwritten by Merrill Lynch & Co if approved, has met stiff resistance in the state Legislature.

Whitman had been counting on the deal to generate nearly $600 million of budget savings for the fiscal year beginning July 1. The court decision on school funding and the Legislature's reluctance to pass the bond deal have threatened to open a large gap in next year's budget.
Relieving the problem to some extent have been strong tax revenue collections, which are exceeding expectations by several hundred million dollars.

In announcing plans to increase school spending, Whitman also said she would pledge rigorous oversight and audits to ensure the new money is spent "in the classroom" and not on new layers of bureaucracy.
